note: Advanced interval singing: each hard leap is found from a neighbour the singer already hears (the high Do for the 7ths, Sol for the tritone and the minor 6th), then one interval-singer is taken up by a Stage selector: the leaps of the major scale, then every hard leap up and down from a new Do. The text names the Stage selector and what the next stage adds, never a level. Folded in from the first-week copy of the same drill.

exercise.title: The hard leaps: 7ths, tritone, minor 6th
exercise.why: A hard leap lands in tune when you first hear a note you already know right beside it, so each one is found from a neighbour: the high Do for the 7ths, Sol for the tritone and the minor 6th.

cells.text:
Press Start below to hear Do and start the mic. The leap to sing shows by name: m7 is a minor 7th up from Do, M7 a major 7th.
Hear the high Do in your head first: the major 7th lands a half step under it, the minor 7th a whole step under it. Then sing that note on "oo" and hold it until Yes shows, and press Next below for another leap.
Practice until the high Do sounds in your head before you sing.
When Do moves to a new key, each 7th is still the same distance under the high Do.

Press Start below to hear Do. The leaps are now TT, the tritone, and m6, the minor 6th.
Hear Sol in your head first: the tritone lands a half step under it, the minor 6th a half step above it. Then sing that note on "oo" and hold it until Yes shows.
If a note won't come, press Show me below to hear it, then press Restart below to sing the same leap again.

Press Start below to hear Do. The first stage asks the leaps of the major scale, to settle your ear.
When each leap lands on your first try, try the next stage: it asks the 7ths, the tritone, the minor 6th and the minor 3rd, down as well as up, from a new Do each time. Use the Stage selector below to change the stage, then press Start to hear Do again.
If a leap down misses, press Restart and hear the landing note in your head before you sing.
